name: ComfyUI — text to music (MiniMax Music 3)
description: ComfyUI preloaded with MiniMax Music 3 for full songs from text: a caption describing the sound plus lyrics with section tags produce a complete 32 kHz stereo track, vocals and arrangement together in one pass, up to about 5 minutes. Two boxes drive it and they do different jobs. The caption is the whole sound and is written in three sections in a fixed order — Global Metadata (genre, BPM, key, mood, use case, production texture), Vocal Details (voice type, delivery, harmonies) and Arrangement (instruments, and what happens across intro, verses, instrumentals, bridge and outro); specific beats poetic, so '78 BPM, D flat major, jazzy extensions' lands where 'dreamy' alone does not, and the shipped lo-fi hip-hop example is there to be edited rather than replaced with an empty box. The lyrics box carries the words plus [Intro] [Verse] [Chorus] [Bridge] [Instrumental] [Outro] tags, and those tags are the only structural instruction the model actually executes — the lyric text itself only conveys mood, and an [Instrumental] tag with nothing under it is how you get a stretch with no singing. max_duration ships at 60 s so the first Run finishes quickly; the model supports up to ~300 s and may also end a song early on its own, and longer costs both time and VRAM. Tiled decode ships on: it decodes the audio VAE in overlapping tiles, which is what keeps a long song inside a 24 GB card, at a small risk of a seam at a tile boundary — turn it off on a big card for the last of the quality. Seed is fixed per take, so the same caption and lyrics with a new seed is a new performance rather than a variation on the old one. Weights are 14.3 GB (4.9 GB fp16 DiT, 9.2 GB pruned int8 text encoder, 0.2 GB audio VAE) and the three loader nodes carry their own HuggingFace URLs, so the launch script fetches exactly what the graph loads and nothing else. Select a persistent-storage bucket on launch: it holds ComfyUI's whole base directory, so those 14.3 GB download once instead of on every launch, and songs are written to the bucket root as song_00001_.mp3, song_00002_.mp3 (the save counter never overwrites, so every take is kept) where the storage API's listFiles, which sees top-level files only, can find them. Without a bucket everything lands in /tmp and is discarded on stop. This is not a chat or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and it is deliberately not vLLM: the upstream MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-Music3 checkpoint is a modular diffusion pipeline whose model_type minimax_music3 Transformers does not recognise, so vLLM exits at config parse — Comfy-Org's repackaging of the same weights is what runs here. Needs a CUDA GPU with 24 GB+ VRAM.
outcome: Turn a style caption and lyrics into a finished song with vocals, up to 5 minutes.

includes.name: MiniMax Music 3 text encoder (pruned, int8 convrot)

workflows.name: Caption + lyrics → song
workflows.description: Write a caption describing the sound and lyrics with [Verse] / [Chorus] section tags, press Run, and a finished song with vocals lands in the bucket root as song_00001_.mp3. The caption takes three sections in order — Global Metadata, Vocal Details, Arrangement — and the section tags in the lyrics are the only structural instruction the model executes. max_duration ships at 60 s (up to ~300 s supported), tiled VAE decode ships on so long songs fit a 24 GB card, and the seed is fixed per take so a take can be reproduced.

requiredResources.description: One CUDA GPU with 24 GB+ VRAM. The weight set is 14.3 GB, so a 24 GB card holds it with room for activations and the launch script's 3/2 rule adds --highvram on anything from 24 GB up, keeping the models resident instead of re-staging them every step. Tiled audio VAE decode, on by default, is what keeps a 5-minute song's decode inside that envelope. Ask for one card and not two: a single sampling pass runs on one device, core ComfyUI has no tensor parallelism, and a second card would be billed while idle.
